links.outcome: Subgroup disparity in suicidal ideation detection between alexithymia and non-alexithymia groups
links.effect: Alexithymia group had decreased likelihood of true detection of suicidal ideation (OR = 0.31, p < .001) with the topic-general classifier; family-related words (p = .02) mediated the disparity.
links.quote: Results showed subgroup disparity in topic-general classifier between alexithymia and non-alexithymia groups at which alexithymia group was associated with a decreased likelihood of true detection of suicidal ideation (OR = 0.31, p < .001) and unique language features, such as family-related words (p = .02), played a mediating/explanatory role.

links.outcome: Effect of topic-specific classifiers on subgroup disparity and overall AUC
links.effect: Topic-specific classifiers achieved AUC = 0.96 versus 0.83 for the topic-general classifier, and the subgroup disparity was largely reduced.
links.quote: Furthermore, topic-specific classifiers demonstrated superior performance (AUC = 0.96) compared to topic-general classifier (AUC = 0.83) and the subgroup disparity was largely reduced.

unlisted_practices: Training topic-specific (factorization) models on specific transcript sections to improve generalizability and equity when patient characteristics are inaccessible
Mediation analysis of language features to explain subgroup performance disparity

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates LLM classifiers for suicidal ideation detection across clinical transcript subgroups to identify equity and generalizability disparities (specifically alexithymia). It is an offline evaluation of model architectures/training subsets rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard.
